newsitem.title: UK: Sottish Amicable says considers three final offers.
newsitem.headline: Sottish Amicable says considers three final offers.

text.p: Hotly-pursued mutal life insurance group Scottish Amicable said on Monday it had received three final offers from its most avid British and Australian suitors by a deadline on last Friday evening and would make its choice by the end of March.
In a statement it confirmed the three offers had come from high street bank Abbey National Plc and from insurers Prudential Corp Plc and Australian Mutual Provident(AMP).

"None of the three parties has asked for their proposals to be made public," ScotAm said, meaning that it will be able to continue to assess the bids under its preferred conditions of full confidentiality.

"The three offers will require detailed actuarial, financial and legal analysis before the board decides upon its recommendation," it added, saying it was confident the board would be able to announce "its recommended proposal" by the end of March.

AMP, Abbey and the Pru are all that are left of half a dozen companies, including National Westminster Bank and Lloyds TSB who last month signed confidentiality agreements with ScotAm to evaluate the company as a takeover prospect.

The final price -- widely expected to top 2.0 billion pounds($3.2 billion) -- is said to have deterred many from taking their interest further and Lloyds admitted recently that after running the slide rule over ScotAm, it felt the bid premium looked too high.
Both the Pru and Abbey have already said that their original proposals might be increased once they had access to more detailed financial detail on ScotAm.
Abbey's original bid was worth up to 1.4 billion pounds while the Pru's 1.9 billion pound offer included a loan element to bolster ScotAm's life fund.
ScotAm, based in Stirling, central Scotland, has arranged for an independent tribunal to resolve any dispute arising from the the takeover battle.
The board has repeatedly stressed that the interests of its 1.1 million policyholders will be uppermost in its final decision. ($ = 0.624 British Pounds)
